title: Top AI Coding Agents and Development Platforms in 2026
description: Comprehensive guide covering the rise of autonomous AI engineers and agentic IDEs in 2026. The industry is seeing a major shift toward developers managing AI agents that write code for them, rather than writing it directly. Highlights that AI coding tools can now write up to 80% of code according to OpenAI President Greg Brockman, though human review and security checks remain critical. The ecosystem now features over 500 LLM models across commercial APIs and open-source releases, with focus shifting from basic code completion to sophisticated AI development partners.
author: MarkTechPost

title: OpenAI Launches Lockdown Mode to Prevent Data Exfiltration
description: OpenAI released Lockdown Mode to help prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. This directly addresses the 'Lethal Trifecta' (private data access + untrusted content exposure + data exfiltration vectors) by cutting off the exfiltration leg. Simon Willison notes this implies ChatGPT's default settings don't provide robust protection against determined data exfiltration attacks.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Enthusiasts vs. Skeptics: Race Against Time vs. Entropy
description: Charity Majors captures the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics: enthusiasts race against time as teams that don't adopt AI could face existential threats from competitors, while skeptics race against entropy as shipping code faster than engineers can read degrades reliability and institutional knowledge. The key issue is there's no natural feedback loop connecting the two groups.
author: Simon Willison (citing Charity Majors)
